title: Find the leaking cable core with a hand-crank insulation tester
instruction: One core of this cable has failed insulation. Find it with the hand-crank insulation tester and its red probe (the tester only reads while its handle is being cranked), push the flag beside that core over to red, put the probe back in its holder and let go of everything.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00, also 49-2092.00) test a cable's cores with a hand-crank insulation tester, which makes its test voltage only while the generator handle turns and drops the reading when cranking stops. One hand cranks while the other holds the line probe on the conductor, so the reading needs both hands at once and the prod moves from core to core while the crank keeps turning. The result is a diagnosis (read the needle, then mark the failed core), not just a hold or a turn.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table top. Insulation tester: fixed steel case 12 x 12 x 12 cm, 3 kg, centred x 30, y -22, with a dial on its near face (needle at 'off' when the handle is still, red band below 1 megohm). On top a vertical-axis hand crank: 4.5 cm bar ending in a free-spinning black knob 2.5 cm across and 3 cm tall (centre 15 cm high); the circle of the knob runs x 25.5 to 34.5. Crank friction 0.03 N m (0.7 N at the knob), no flywheel; the knob starts at y -17.5. Terminal block: wooden plate 14 x 22 x 3 cm, 3 kg, at x 30, y 14, with three brass test studs 2.5 cm across, tops 6 cm high, at y +6, +14 and +22 (plain posts, nothing to clip to). Behind each stud at x 35 a toggle flag: 5 cm lever with a 2.5 cm green tab on a pin 3 cm high, upright (green) or tipped 40 degrees away from the robot (red), 0.04 N m detent. Red test prod: 2.5 cm grip, 12 cm long, with a 3 cm tip of 1.2 cm across, 0.06 kg, standing tip-down in a holder cup (flared mouth) at x 24, y +28, grip centre 10 cm high. The faulty core is the middle one (y +14, reads 0.5 megohm); the other two read infinity.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a stopwatch. A core counts as tested when the prod's tip rests on its stud (within 2 mm of the top and 6.5 mm of the axis, prod within 30 degrees of vertical) for 1 s while the crank turns at 0.4 rev/s or more (speed over the last 0.5 s). 0 at once and for good if a flag is pushed to red before all three cores were tested, a flag is pushed on a healthy core, the prod is dropped (falls over or lies low away from its holder), or a gripper touches a stud; also 0 if no core was tested. Otherwise 0.25 for one or two cores tested; 0.5 for all three tested but the faulty core's flag not at red; 0.75 for all three tested and only the middle flag at red, but the prod not back in its holder (within 1 cm and 10 degrees), a gripper within 3 cm of the prod, knob or flags, or not still; 1.0 with all of that met and the prod, flags and crank still (1 mm, 1 degree) for 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the prod in its holder, turn the crank so the knob is at y -17.5, tip all three flags back to green, set the needle to off.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; the crank is a revolute joint with 0.03 N m Coulomb friction, the flags are hinges with a drive detent. The test voltage, 1 s timer, needle and readings are computed in code. The prod's lead is not simulated; the earth lead is not modelled. No electricity.
